model_rule: .converge/playbooks/ is source blueprint; .converge/journal/ is executable run state/evidence. Fix source or loader/compiler behavior; do not hand-edit manifest.json or runstate.json.

findings.gap: compilePlaybook falls back to reading manifest.json from .converge/journal/ when target manifest is missing. Journal is runtime state/evidence, not a compilation source. Stale or corrupted journal state can infect the DAG.
findings.evidence: run/index.ts:1243: constant journal path join(projectDir, '.converge', 'journal', playbookName, 'manifest.json') — reads journal artifact as compilation input
findings.correction: Remove the journal manifest fallback at lines 1242-1245. When target manifest is missing, recompile from playbook source instead of reading journal artifacts.
findings.test_to_write: tests/compile-does-not-read-journal.test.ts — compile a playbook, delete target manifest, corrupt journal manifest, recompile, and verify DAG matches playbook source not corrupted journal

findings.gap: Task content resolution prefers runstate.json (runtime state) over filesystem TASK.md (playbook source). If they diverge, the stale journal wins, violating the rule that playbook source is authoritative.
findings.evidence: run/index.ts:968: comment explicitly states 'Prefer task content from runstate.json (embedded at compile time). Fall back to filesystem TASK.md only when task_def is unavailable.' — inverts the blueprint/runtime priority
findings.correction: Invert the priority: prefer playbook source TASK.md, and fall back to runstate.json embedded content only for spawned (runtime-created) tasks that have no playbook source.
findings.test_to_write: tests/task-content-source-priority.test.ts — create a playbook TASK.md, compile, then modify the journal runstate.json content. Verify execution uses playbook source, not stale runstate.

findings.gap: The repair prompts correctly enforce the blueprint/runtime boundary on users (journal files are READ-ONLY, edit playbook source), but compile-time code (run/index.ts:1243, run/index.ts:968) violates the same boundary by reading journal artifacts as compilation sources.
findings.evidence: context-writer.ts:198: 'Journal files are READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit them — they will be overwritten on the next attempt.' vs run/index.ts:1243 reading journal manifest as compilation fallback — the framework enforces a boundary it does not itself respect
findings.correction: After fixing findings 1 and 2, audit all remaining code paths that read from journal/ at compile time. Any journal reads in compilation paths should be replaced with playbook source reads or explicit compile-from-source logic.
findings.test_to_write: tests/no-journal-reads-during-compile.test.ts — instrument all compilation code paths to assert no journal/ reads occur during manifest generation
